title: Composite body: response of two bound bodies to a uniform cost gradient

key_results.statement: The changes of the data $(t^{(i)},K^{(i)},W)$ that leave $C$ unchanged are $\delta K^{(1)}_h=Z+\alpha_h$, $\delta K^{(2)}_k=-Z+\beta_k$, $\delta t^{(1)}_{hh}=\tau_h$, $\delta t^{(2)}_{kk}=\tau'_k$, $\delta W_{hk}=-(\tau_h+\alpha_h)-(\tau'_k+\beta_k)$ with $Z=Z^\dagger$ on $\mathcal H_c$ and real $\alpha_h,\beta_k,\tau_h,\tau'_k$; the family contains the split (16.3) and all placements of single-object terms (A5), and $\bar R$, $A$ and $\mu_c$ are invariant under it and, up to the global isometry $R_\theta:v\mapsto e^{i\theta}v$ of the background, under the common phase.

Under a change of the split (16.3), $\bar x_1-\bar x_2\mapsto\bar x_1-\bar x_2+2z$ with $z=(Z-\langle Z\rangle)\chi$, and every $z$ with $\langle\chi\vert z\rangle=0$ occurs, so $\bar x_1-\bar x_2$ and each of its components are not well defined; differences within one body, such as $\Delta^{(i)}$ and $\bar x_i(\lambda)-\bar x_i(0)$, are well defined.

(20.6)–(20.7) apply to each body, with the other body and the medium as companion, so for every $\lambda$: $A(\lambda)=\tfrac12\sum_{i=1,2}\sum_{\{h,h'\}\in E_i}\bigl[A^{(i)}_{hh'}(\lambda)+B^{(i)}_{hh'}(\lambda)\bigr]\Delta^{(i)}_{hh'}$, where $A^{(i)}_{hh'}$ contains the hopping terms and $B^{(i)}_{hh'}$ the on-site, record and binding terms.

$W$ appears explicitly in $A(\lambda)$ only through $A_W(\lambda)=\tfrac12\bigl[\sum_{E_1}w^{(1)}_{hh'}\Delta^{(1)}_{hh'}+\sum_{E_2}w^{(2)}_{kk'}\Delta^{(2)}_{kk'}\bigr]$ with $w^{(1)}_{hh'}=2\operatorname{Re}\bigl[t^{(1)}_{hh'}\langle\psi^{(1)}_h\vert(W_{h\cdot}-W_{h'\cdot})\otimes\mathbb 1_c\vert\psi^{(1)}_{h'}\rangle\bigr]$ and $w^{(2)}_{kk'}$ likewise; for $\lambda>0$ every term also depends on $W$ implicitly through $\Psi(\lambda)$.

At $\lambda=0$, $A(0)=\tfrac12\sum_{i=1,2}\bigl[a^{(i)}_{\rm hop}+\sum_{E_i}(\Omega^{(i)}_h-\Omega^{(i)}_{h'})L^{(i)}_{hh'}(0)\Delta^{(i)}_{hh'}\bigr]+A_W(0)$, with the hopping terms $a^{(i)}_{\rm hop}$ and $\Omega^{(i)}_h=t^{(i)}_{hh}+\epsilon^{(i)}_h$; every term except $A_W(0)$ depends on $\Phi$ only through the views $\rho_i$.

If $\ell^{(1)}_{hh';k}(W_{hk}-W_{h'k})=0$ for all $\{h,h'\}\in E_1$ and all $k$, and $\ell^{(2)}_{kk';h}(W_{hk}-W_{hk'})=0$ for all $\{k,k'\}\in E_2$ and all $h$, then $A_W(0)=0$: no edge cost resolved by the place of the other body sits on a hop across which the binding changes, for example when $\Phi$ is a single joint place.

For an eigenvector $\Phi$ of $C_{\rm body}$ the edge identity $w^{(1)}_{hh'}(0)=-A^{(1)}_{hh'}(0)-(t^{(1)}_{hh}-t^{(1)}_{h'h'})L^{(1)}_{hh'}(0)$ holds on every edge of $E_1$ (likewise for $b_2$), so the $W$-terms are cancelled by the hopping and on-site terms, and $A_W(0)=0$ if and only if $\sum_i\bigl[a^{(i)}_{\rm hop}+\sum_{E_i}(t^{(i)}_{hh}-t^{(i)}_{h'h'})L^{(i)}_{hh'}(0)\Delta^{(i)}_{hh'}\bigr]=0$.

The inverse inertia of the composite exists, is unique and equals $\mu_c=-\tfrac14\sum_{i=1,2}\sum_{\{h,h'\}\in E_i}L^{(i)}_{hh'}(0)\Delta^{(i)}_{hh'}\,g(\Delta^{(i)}_{hh'},\cdot)=\tfrac14(\mu_1+\mu_2)$, so it depends on the edge costs $L^{(1)}(0)$, $L^{(2)}(0)$ and the backgrounds alone, has no explicit dependence on $W$ (which enters only through $\Phi$), and is $g$-symmetric.

$\mu_c$ is positive semidefinite if and only if $\sum_{i=1,2}\sum_{E_i}L^{(i)}_{hh'}(0)\,g(\Delta^{(i)}_{hh'},v)^2\le0$ for all $v\in\mathcal H_c$; a sufficient condition is $L^{(i)}_{hh'}(0)\le0$ on every edge with $\Delta^{(i)}_{hh'}\neq0$.

On the chain, for $t>0$ and $U<0$, $C_{\rm body}$ has one bound state per total quasi-momentum $K$, $E_b(K)=-\sqrt{U^2+16t^2\cos^2(K/2)}$, below the two-body continuum at that $K$, $[-4t\lvert\cos(K/2)\rvert,4t\lvert\cos(K/2)\rvert]$; hence $\operatorname{spec}C_{\rm body}=[-4t,4t]\cup\bigl[-\sqrt{U^2+16t^2},-\lvert U\rvert\bigr]$ and $E_{\min}(t,U)=-\sqrt{U^2+16t^2}$; at $U=0$ there is no bound state and $E_{\min}=-4t$.

For $t>0$, $\sigma_X>0$ and $U\le0$, along every sequence of finite-support starts $\Phi_n\otimes\chi$ with $\langle\Phi_n\vert C_{\rm body}\vert\Phi_n\rangle\to E_{\min}(t,U)$, $\mu_c\to I_c^{-1}\hat e\,g(\hat e,\cdot)$ independently of the sequence, with $I_c(t,U,\sigma_X)=\sqrt{U^2+16t^2}/(4t^2\sigma_X^2)$; for one body, along starts with $\langle C_1\rangle\to\inf\operatorname{spec}C_1=-2t$, $I_1=1/(2t\sigma_X^2)$, and $I_c(t,0,\sigma_X)=1/(t\sigma_X^2)=2I_1$, so $I_c/(2I_1)=\sqrt{1+U^2/(16t^2)}$ and $I_c>2I_1$ for $U<0$.

$I_c-2I_1=-E_{\rm bind}/v_{\max}^2$ with $E_{\rm bind}=E_{\min}(t,U)-E_{\min}(t,0)<0$ and $v_{\max}=2t\sigma_X$, so $I_c-2I_1$ is a function of $E_{\rm bind}$ and $v_{\max}$ alone and the binding raises the inertia; the relation is invariant under $C\to C+c\,\mathbb 1$ when the same $c$ is added in the same placement at $U$ and at $U=0$.

$I_c\,v_{\max}^2=\sqrt{U^2+16t^2}=-E_{\min}(t,U)$, a function of $E_{\min}$ alone, in the normalization of the example (zero diagonal of $C_1$ and $C_2$, $W=0$ off $m=n$); it is not invariant under $C\to C+c\,\mathbb 1$ when $c$ is placed in $C_{\rm body}$, because $E_{\min}\to E_{\min}+c$ while $I_c$ and $v_{\max}$ are unchanged.

Along the minimizing sequences of (21.15), $A_W(0)\to0$, bounded by a multiple of $\sqrt{\langle\Phi\vert\Gamma\vert\Phi\rangle}$ with $\Gamma=C_{\rm body}-E_{\min}\ge0$; since $A(0)-\mu_cF_{\rm tot}=A_W(0)$ exactly for every start of finite support, $\lim A(0)=\lim\mu_cF_{\rm tot}=-8t^2\langle X\rangle e/\sqrt{U^2+16t^2}$.

open_issues: The inverse inertia of the composite is the response at λ = 0 only; whether the composite then moves as one body for λ > 0 is out of scope.
The separation of two bodies recorded in one medium is not defined (21.3); a relative position would need structure beyond this setting.
The split of A(0) into A_W and the rest, and E_min itself, depend on the placement convention (A5); only A(0), μ_c and E_bind (under a common shift) are invariant.
Relation (21.16) is established only for the chain example.

consistency_checks.check: U = 0 (two independent bodies): each one-body hopping expectation tends to −2t, so (21.10) gives I_c = 2I₁, in agreement with (21.15) at U = 0, and the W-terms vanish identically.
Strong binding |U| ≫ t: the bound band reduces to a single body on the pair places with hopping 2t²/U that feels the total force, and its one-body inertia |U|/(4t²σ_X²) is the limit of (21.15).
Dimensions: with [C] = [λ]⁻¹ = ν, both μ_c in (21.10) and the inverse of I_c in (21.15) scale as ν³, and both sides of (21.16) scale as ν⁻³.
